If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid over-optimism.

If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecasted price by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to counteract pessimism.

If sentiment shifts from positive to negative mid-horizon (day 8–15), reduce forecast by 1–2% in the next 3–5 days to reflect sentiment reversal.

If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, slightly increase forecast by 0.5–1% for mid-horizon (8–15 days) to capture momentum.

If sentiment is mixed and price is trending downward, slightly decrease forecast by 0.5–1% for mid-horizon (8–15 days) to avoid underestimating downside risk.

If sentiment is neutral or volatile (≤0.33 or ≥0.67) in late horizon (16–30 days), apply no adjustment unless true price deviates >1.5% from forecast — then adjust by ±1% to align with recent sentiment drift.
